articles.title: Conservationist honoured for protecting rare animals
articles.summary: Tullis Matson runs Nature's SAFE, a charity that has been freezing cells from some of the world's most endangered animals
articles.content:
A conservationist who set up a wildlife conservation charity has said being given an honorary degree is the "highlight" of his year.

Tullis Matson, who stores biological samples in a 'time capsule' to help protect endangered species from going extinct, said he was particularly thrilled with the award marking his achievements as he is "very dyslexic" and "left school with no qualifications".

He is among a cohort of seven people to be given the award by Shropshire's Harper Adams University as part of its 125th anniversary celebrations.

Comedian Ed Byrne and The Archers actress Felicity Finch are part of the group receiving their degrees this month.

Matson, who is from Whitchurch, runs Nature's SAFE, a charity that has been freezing cells from some of the world's most endangered animals.

He also founded and leads Stallion Artificial Insemination Services, a world-leading company that specialises in cryopreservation technology.

"The journey through my education was really tough," he said.

"So now to get this is quite incredible, I'm absolutely blown away."
articles.reasoning: The article highlights a conservationist honored for his impactful work in protecting endangered species through cryopreservation, which has broad environmental significance and tangible benefits for biodiversity preservation.
articles.personality_title: Conservationist honored for protecting endangered animals with cell freezing
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Some animals around the world are disappearing and might become extinct. To help save them, scientists and conservationists look for ways to protect these species and keep their populations healthy.

**What happened** – Tullis Matson, a conservationist from Whitchurch, was given an honorary degree by Harper Adams University. He runs a charity called Nature's SAFE that freezes cells from endangered animals. This process, called cryopreservation, stores animal cells safely so they can be used in the future to help bring animals back or increase their numbers. Matson also leads a company that specializes in this technology. He says receiving the degree is a big moment for him because he struggled in school due to dyslexia.

**Impact** – Matson’s work is important because freezing animal cells creates a kind of “time capsule” that can protect species from disappearing forever. This helps scientists save animals even if their natural populations shrink or vanish. His efforts show how technology can support wildlife conservation in new ways.

**What's next step** – The honorary degree may help Matson gain more support and attention for his charity and technology. This could lead to more funding and partnerships to freeze cells from other endangered animals, increasing the chances of saving more species.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Tullis Matson’s use of cell freezing is a valuable tool helping protect endangered animals, earning him recognition despite early learning challenges.
articles.personality_title_fr: Un conservationniste honoré pour la protection des animaux en voie de disparition grâce à la congélation de cellules
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Certains animaux dans le monde disparaissent et risquent de s’éteindre. Pour les sauver, les scientifiques et les conservateurs cherchent des méthodes pour protéger ces espèces et maintenir leurs populations.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Tullis Matson, un conservateur de Whitchurch, a reçu un diplôme honorifique de l’université Harper Adams. Il dirige une association appelée Nature's SAFE qui congèle des cellules d’animaux en voie de disparition. Cette technique, appelée cryoconservation, permet de stocker les cellules en toute sécurité pour les utiliser plus tard afin d’aider à restaurer ou augmenter les populations animales. Matson dirige aussi une entreprise spécialisée dans cette technologie. Il explique que ce diplôme est très important pour lui car il a eu des difficultés à l’école à cause de sa dyslexie.

**Impact** – Le travail de Matson est important car la congélation des cellules crée une sorte de « capsule temporelle » qui protège les espèces de la disparition totale. Cela aide les scientifiques à sauver des animaux même si leurs populations naturelles diminuent ou disparaissent. Ses efforts montrent comment la technologie peut soutenir la conservation de la faune.

**Prochaine étape** – Ce diplôme honorifique pourrait aider Matson à obtenir plus de soutien et d’attention pour son association et sa technologie. Cela pourrait permettre d’obtenir plus de financements et de partenariats pour congeler les cellules d’autres animaux en danger, augmentant ainsi les chances de sauver plus d’espèces.

**Résumé en une phrase** – L’utilisation par Tullis Matson de la congélation de cellules est un outil précieux pour protéger les animaux en voie de disparition, lui valant une reconnaissance malgré ses difficultés scolaires.
articles.personality_title_es: Conservacionista reconocido por proteger animales en peligro mediante congelación de células
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Algunos animales en el mundo están desapareciendo y podrían extinguirse. Para ayudarlos, científicos y conservacionistas buscan formas de proteger estas especies y mantener sus poblaciones.

**Qué pasó** – Tullis Matson, un conservacionista de Whitchurch, recibió un título honorífico de la Universidad Harper Adams. Él dirige una organización llamada Nature's SAFE que congela células de animales en peligro. Esta técnica, llamada criopreservación, guarda las células de forma segura para usarlas en el futuro y ayudar a recuperar o aumentar las poblaciones animales. Matson también lidera una empresa que se especializa en esta tecnología. Dice que recibir este título es muy importante para él porque tuvo dificultades en la escuela debido a la dislexia.

**Impacto** – El trabajo de Matson es importante porque congelar células crea una especie de «cápsula del tiempo» que puede proteger a las especies de desaparecer para siempre. Esto ayuda a los científicos a salvar animales, incluso si sus poblaciones naturales disminuyen o desaparecen. Su trabajo muestra cómo la tecnología puede apoyar la conservación de la vida silvestre.

**Próximo paso** – El título honorífico podría ayudar a Matson a obtener más apoyo y atención para su organización y tecnología. Esto podría traer más fondos y colaboraciones para congelar células de otros animales en peligro, aumentando las posibilidades de salvar más especies.

**Resumen en una frase** – El uso de la congelación de células por parte de Tullis Matson es una herramienta valiosa que ayuda a proteger animales en peligro y le ha ganado reconocimiento a pesar de sus dificultades escolares.
